_meta.name: AlmiOET UK professions block — medicine, pharmacy, physiotherapy — v1 (dentistry documented as EXCLUDED)
_meta.purpose: Opens the PROFESSIONS axis on the proven UK destination. Each is a profession-specific UK regulator + OET requirement + registration pathway — supports rich 'OET for {profession}: {regulator}' recognition pages now, and profession corridors later (which will also need profession-specific ORIGIN regulators, e.g. PM&DC for Pakistani doctors — not yet sourced).
_meta.oet_honesty: Confirmed OET-accepting UK professions here: medicine (GMC), pharmacy (GPhC), physiotherapy (HCPC). EXCLUDED: dentistry (GDC) — the GDC's official English-language-controls guidance names ONLY IELTS (overall 7.0, 6.5 each); OET is not listed. Blogs claiming the GDC accepts OET are uncorroborated by the regulator. Do NOT build an OET-dentistry-UK page without confirming acceptance directly with the GDC. (See dentistryExcluded below.)
_meta.reuse_note: Country-level attestation base + English-medium status from v4 origins reuse for these professions (they are country-level, not profession-specific). What differs per profession: the ORIGIN professional regulator (nursing council vs medical/dental/pharmacy council) and the DESTINATION regulator + exam + OET version. Origin professional regulators are the next gather.
_meta.sourcing: All from official regulator sites (gmc-uk.org, pharmacyregulation.org, hcpc-uk.org) + GOV.UK. Fees/visa periodically revised → confirm-official.

regulator.value: The General Medical Council (GMC) registers and licenses doctors in the UK; you must be registered AND hold a licence to practise. International medical graduates apply for full registration with a licence to practise.

englishOET.value: The GMC accepts OET — doctors take the OET MEDICINE version and need Grade B in each of the four sub-tests, all in the same sitting (grades can't be combined across sittings), valid two years. Alternative: IELTS Academic overall 7.5 with at least 7.0 in each skill.

registrationPathway.value: International medical graduates reach full registration via: (1) PLAB — pass PLAB Part 1 and Part 2 (within two years), plus an acceptable primary medical qualification and internship; (2) an acceptable GMC-approved postgraduate qualification (exempts from PLAB); or (3) sponsorship by a GMC-approved body. All routes also require English evidence, primary-source verification of the qualification, and a certificate of good standing from each regulator held.

verification.value: The GMC requires primary source verification (PSV) of the primary medical qualification, carried out by ECFMG (Intealth) via its EPIC service, which confirms the qualification with the awarding institution directly; plus a certificate of good standing from each medical regulator the doctor has registered with.

fees.value: GMC (April 2025 figures; revised each April — confirm current): full registration with a licence £463 (+£463/yr retention); low-income discounts apply. PLAB Part 1 £273; PLAB Part 2 £998.

professions.oetRole: Yes — OET Medicine, Grade B in all four, one sitting.
searchWording: GMC registration without PLAB postgraduate qualification

regulator.value: The General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC) is the statutory regulator for pharmacists in Great Britain (Pharmacy Order 2010); registration is required to practise as a pharmacist.

englishOET.value: The GPhC accepts OET — Grade B in each of the four areas at one sitting (OET on Paper or on Computer; OET@Home not accepted). Alternative: IELTS Academic overall 7 with no area below 7.

sources.name: GPhC — evidence of English language skills (June 2025)

registrationPathway.value: Internationally-qualified pharmacists: (1) eligibility assessment of the overseas qualification (fee; eligibility letter valid two academic years); (2) the Overseas Pharmacists' Assessment Programme (OSPAP), a one-year GPhC-accredited postgraduate conversion diploma; (3) 52 weeks of foundation training in Great Britain; (4) pass the common registration assessment; (5) join Part 1 of the register. English and fitness-to-practise requirements also apply.

sources.name: GPhC — registering as an internationally qualified pharmacist (April 2025)

verification.value: The GPhC verifies overseas qualifications through the eligibility assessment before OSPAP; where a degree isn't equivalent to a UK bachelor's it assesses the syllabus via its international comparative assessment framework. Registration is confirmed on the GPhC online register.

fees.value: GPhC (July 2025 Fees Rules): eligibility assessment £783 (non-refundable); application to enter Part 1 £489 (→£518 from 1 Sep 2026); entry completion £293 (→£311); annual renewal £293 (→£311). OSPAP tuition is set by universities, separate.

professions.oetRole: Yes — OET Grade B in all four, one sitting.
searchWording: how to register as a pharmacist in the UK from overseas

regulator.value: The Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) is the UK statutory regulator for physiotherapists (and 15 other professions); registration is required to use the protected title 'Physiotherapist'.

englishOET.value: The HCPC accepts the profession-specific OET (physiotherapy version) — minimum 350 (Grade B) with no element below 300 for most professions including physiotherapy. Alternatives: IELTS 7.0 overall with no element below 6.5, or TOEFL iBT. Certificate under two years old, taken at an official centre.

sources.name: HCPC — certificate of English language proficiency

registrationPathway.value: Internationally-trained physiotherapists apply via the HCPC international application route: an online application including a 'standards of proficiency mapping document' where HCPC assesses education/training against UK standards; where gaps are found the applicant may need a Test of Competence or a Period of Adaptation. Successful applicants join the Register and gain the protected title.

verification.value: Applicants certify supporting documents (qualification certificates/transcripts, English proficiency certificate, professional registration/good-standing evidence, and the standards-of-proficiency mapping document), which the HCPC scrutinises against UK standards to verify equivalence and fitness to register.

fees.value: HCPC international application scrutiny fee: a one-off non-refundable £678.38 for the assessment; a separate periodic registration fee (per two-year cycle) is payable once approved — see HCPC fees pages for the current amount.

dentistryExcluded.reason: The GDC's official Guidance on English language controls names ONLY IELTS (Academic, overall 7.0 with 6.5 in each) as the standardised test — OET is not listed as accepted evidence, unlike the GMC/GPhC/HCPC. So an 'OET → dentist → UK' page cannot honestly tell a dentist OET satisfies the GDC. Excluded from AlmiOET UK corridors unless/until OET acceptance is confirmed directly with the GDC.

sources.name: GDC — Guidance on English language controls (IELTS only)
GDC — Overseas Registration Examination (ORE Part 1 + Part 2)

dentistryExcluded.note: Dentist→UK is still a real REGISTRATION corridor (ORE Part 1 £485, Part 2 ~£6,967 in 2026; ARF £698), just not an OET one. It could live in the broader nursing/health network as an IELTS/ORE page, not an AlmiOET page.
